scenes.heading: Simultaneous equations by substitution
scenes.sub: Two equations, one answer that fits both
scenes.say: When two facts link two unknowns, you need an answer that fits both at once. That's a pair of simultaneous equations, and substitution is a neat way to crack them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A substitute takes the exact place of the player who left
scenes.science: If y = 2x + 1, put (2x + 1) in place of y in the other equation
scenes.breaks: A substitute player is a different person; y and 2x + 1 have exactly the same value.
scenes.say: Think of a substitute in sport. They take the exact place of the player who leaves. If y equals two x plus one, you can take y off and put two x plus one on in its place in the other equation. Now only x is left to solve.

scenes.heading: A solution is a crossing point
scenes.say: Each equation is a straight line. First the line y equals two x plus one, then x plus y equals seven. They cross at two, five. That point is the solution, because it lies on both lines.
scenes.caption: y = 2x + 1 and x + y = 7 cross at (2, 5): the solution.

scenes.heading: The substitution method
steps: Make x or y the subject
scenes.say: Here's the method. Make one pronumeral the subject. Substitute it into the other equation, in brackets. Solve. Then substitute back to find the other value, and check in both equations.

scenes.heading: Rearrange, then substitute
scenes.question: Solve 2x + 3y = 12 and x − 2y = −1.
scenes.say: Rearrange the second equation: x equals two y minus one. Substitute it, in brackets, into the first. Seven y minus two equals twelve, so y is two. Then x equals three. Check: six plus six is twelve.
scenes.caption: x = 2y − 1. Substitute: 2(2y − 1) + 3y = 12, so y = 2 and x = 3.

scenes.heading: Parallel lines: no solution
scenes.say: Watch out for parallel lines. y equals two x plus one and four x minus two y equals six both have gradient two. Substituting gives negative two equals six, which is false. The lines never meet, so there is no solution.
scenes.caption: Both lines have gradient 2. Substitution gives −2 = 6, which is false: no solution.

points: Swap in the expression, in brackets
scenes.say: Recap. The solution is where the lines cross. Substitute in brackets, solve, substitute back and check both equations. A false statement means no solution; always true means infinitely many. Now try the practice questions!
